transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's, um, it's very nice to meet you too. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I'm just here because... well, since I retired—stopped working—I just can't seem to slow down. I'm up and moving from one little job around the house to the next, all day long. It's almost like I still have a crew waiting on me, you know? I just like to stay busy, I suppose. Is that... is that the kind of thing you need to know?
When you are keeping busy like this, do you feel a sense of inner tension or worry that you simply cannot turn off?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't really say it's worry or anything like that. I'm not much of a nervous fellow, honestly. It's not a bad feeling, like tension... I just, well, I just like being productive, I guess. It just feels good to get things done around the house. I hope that makes sense? I'm not trying to be difficult, I just don't think I feel anxious about it. Is it alright if it's just a bit of extra energy?
Do you find that you need less sleep than you used to, yet you still wake up feeling refreshed and ready to go?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I still try to get my usual seven or eight hours, just like I always have. I don't think I'm staying up all hours of the night or anything like that. Sometimes I might wake up a little early, but I think that's just part of getting older, isn't it? I certainly don't feel like I have some kind of superpower where I don't need sleep. I just... I just sleep like a normal fellow my age, I think. Does that sound about right to you?
Do you feel that your need to stay busy ever gets in the way of your ability to enjoy your leisure time or spend time relaxing with your family?

Well, um, I wouldn't say it gets in the way of my family time, exactly. My wife and I still sit down together in the evenings. It's just... well, I suppose I don't do so well with the quiet hobbies for very long anymore. Like, if I sit down to read the paper or maybe do a little sketching, I find myself sort of... humming a bit, or maybe talking to myself, or I'll just pop up to go adjust a picture frame or mess with something on the shelf. I'm not trying to be disruptive, I just... I like to keep a little momentum going, I guess. I hope that doesn't sound too bothersome to be around. Do you think that's fairly normal for a fellow who's used to working hard his whole life?
When you feel the urge to get up and adjust a picture frame or tidy a shelf, do you feel that you *must* do it to prevent something bad from happening or to relieve a strong sense of discomfort?

Oh, heavens no. No, nothing like that at all. I don't... I don't think something terrible is going to happen if a picture is a little crooked. I just like things to look nice, you know? It's just a preference, really. I don't feel any sort of... well, discomfort or anything. I just see something that needs a little straightening, and I just pop over and do it. It's just keeping a tidy house, I suppose. I hope I haven't made it sound like I'm terribly neurotic or anything. I just like to be helpful around the place, is all. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any recent changes in your memory, such as forgetting the names of familiar people or where you have placed your personal belongings?

Well, I... I wouldn't say my memory is going bad, not like, you know, forgetting who people are or anything serious like that. My mind's still sharp as a tack for the important things! But, um, I suppose I do spend a little more time than I'd like hunting around for things. Just silly things, really. Like my glasses, or my keys, or... oh, I have this little notebook I use to jot down stories and ideas, and my tape measure for when I'm tinkering. I'll set them down, and then I'm walking all over the house trying to figure out where they've gotten to. And the funny thing is, half the time I swear I just had the darn thing in my hand two minutes before! It's a bit embarrassing, really, but I think that's just normal forgetfulness, don't you? Just getting a little sidetracked, I suppose. I hope that doesn't mean anything's really wrong upstairs.
Have your wife or other close friends mentioned that your personality has changed, or that you've been acting differently in social situations lately?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. My wife hasn't said anything about my personality changing, and my friends haven't either. I mean, I'm still the same old me! I might be a little more... energetic, maybe, or a bit more talkative when I get going on a story, but I'm certainly not acting strange or anything. I try very hard to be polite and pleasant when we have company or go out. I'd hate for anyone to think I was being rude or inappropriate. I think I'm still pretty good company, all things considered. I'm just a regular fellow, you know? I hope I'm coming across alright to you today, doctor. I wouldn't want you to think I've gone funny in the head or anything!

When you are working on your projects or tinkering around the house, have you noticed any difficulty in planning out your steps, or perhaps finding that you start one task and then jump to another before the first one is finished?

Well, I... I always try my absolute best to get everything done, I really do. I wouldn't necessarily call it a difficulty with planning, exactly... I think I just get a little overly eager to help out around the place. 

Like, my wife might ask me to do a few little chores outside—maybe fix the gate, sweep the porch, and put the tools away. And I fully intend to do every bit of it for her! But sometimes I'll... well, I'll get the gate about half done, and then I'll spot some weeds over by the steps that need pulling. So I'll just wander off to take care of those right quick, you know, to be extra helpful. And then, well... I suppose I do end up leaving the rest of the chores sitting there unfinished. 

It’s a little embarrassing to admit, if I'm being honest. My wife does have to remind me about the tools and the sweeping. I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or careless! I really do mean well, I just try to do too many good deeds at once and get a little sidetracked. That’s fairly normal for a fellow my age with a lot on his plate, wouldn't you say?
Have you found yourself saying or doing things in public recently that you might have previously considered a bit too blunt or out of character for you?

Oh, my goodness, no. I would never! I pride myself on being polite and respectful, especially out in public. I've always believed in minding my manners and treating people right. 

I mean, I suppose sometimes if I'm really excited about something I might speak up a little quicker than I ought to, or maybe talk a bit louder than necessary... but I'd never say anything rude or hurtful. I'd be absolutely mortified if I ever offended anyone or made a scene. I try very hard to be a gentleman, doctor. I hope you haven't gotten the impression that I'm the sort of person who just blurts out inappropriate things. I'm doing alright in that department, aren't I?

When you have these moments where you move from one task to another, do you ever feel like your mind is 'slipping' or that you are struggling to keep track of the steps required to complete a multi-step project, even when you are trying your hardest to focus?

Oh, no, it's nothing like that, doctor. My mind isn't slipping, I promise you. I'm sharp as a tack! I don't ever feel confused or like I'm losing track of things because I can't remember the steps. 

It's more just... well, like I said, I just get a little too eager to get everything done at once. I'll be working on something and then I'll just spot something else that needs doing, and I just want to jump right on it to be helpful. It's not that I don't know how to finish the first thing, I just... I guess my attention just gets pulled away by wanting to do a good job on the next thing, too. 

I'm certainly not struggling to think straight or anything like that. I really do try my hardest to focus, and I think I do a pretty good job of it most of the time. I'm just a busy bee, that's all! You don't think that sounds like my mind is slipping, do you? I'm sure it's just a normal thing to get a little distracted when you're trying to be as helpful as you can.
Have you or your wife noticed any changes in your balance, the way you walk, or any new stiffness in your muscles lately?

Oh, no, definitely not. My balance is just fine, and I'm walking as well as I ever have! I make sure to keep active, you know, moving around the house and the yard. I don't feel stiff or anything like that. 

I mean, I suppose anyone my age gets a little bit of the normal aches and pains when they wake up, but nothing out of the ordinary, and certainly nothing that slows me down or makes me stumble. I'm very careful on my feet. I'd hate for my wife to worry about me falling or anything! 

So, no, nothing like that at all. I'm holding up pretty well physically, wouldn't you say? I always try to take good care of myself.

If you had to follow a written set of instructions, like a recipe for a new dish or a guide for assembling a piece of furniture, would you find that you have any more trouble following those steps in order than you did a few years ago?

Oh, heavens no. I can still follow a set of instructions just fine. If my wife asks me to help out with a new recipe, or if we get a little piece of patio furniture that needs putting together, I can read through the steps just like I always have. 

I mean, sometimes... well, sometimes I might try to skip ahead a step or two, but that's just because I think I know how it goes and I want to get it done quickly for her. Just trying to be helpful and efficient, you know? But if I really need to sit down and read step one, step two, step three... I don't have any trouble with that at all. Certainly not any more than I did five or ten years ago. 

I can still follow along perfectly well when I put my mind to it. That's a good sign, isn't it, doctor? I always try to make sure I'm doing things the right way.
Have you noticed if you have had any more trouble than usual keeping track of your daily appointments or managing your household finances lately?

Oh, well... maybe just a tiny bit, but nothing to be worried about, I promise! I mean, I've always tried to be very responsible with our affairs. I suppose lately, I might have had a few little slip-ups... just minor things, really. 

Like, I've forgotten to return a couple of calls from the community center, or... well, I might forget to pay a bill just until my wife reminds me. But she's a wonderful help, and we always get it taken care of right away once she mentions it! And, oh, the other day I did forget to bring the supplies I promised for the garden group. 

But I really think it’s just because I’m trying to be involved in so much and help out wherever I can. I just get so wrapped up in being active. It’s pretty normal to let a little detail slip here and there when you’re trying to be that helpful, isn't it? I’m still managing things just fine overall, doctor, I assure you.
Have you ever been diagnosed with a medical condition, such as a thyroid problem, vitamin deficiency, or any other health issue, that your doctor has been monitoring?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. My doctor says I'm in excellent health, really. I go for my regular checkups, of course, because I want to make sure I'm doing everything I'm supposed to. But no thyroid issues or vitamin problems or anything they need to keep an eye on. 

I take my daily multivitamin just to be safe, you know, trying to be proactive. But as far as any actual medical conditions... no, I've got a clean bill of health. I'm very lucky that way. It's always good to be healthy, right? I try my best to keep it that way.

Have you noticed any times, perhaps in the evening or when you are very tired, where your ability to focus or stay alert seems to drift in and out, making you feel a bit more 'foggy' or disoriented than at other times of the day?

Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say I get disoriented or... or foggy at all. I mean, sure, by the time the evening rolls around, I might be a little physically tired, just from trying to keep busy and, you know, helping my wife around the house all day. But my mind stays perfectly clear, I promise you that. 

I don't drift in and out or lose track of what's going on. I always try to make sure I'm paying attention, even if we're just sitting down to watch a little television after dinner. It's just normal, everyday tiredness, really... and that's completely normal for a fellow my age at the end of a long day, isn't it? But no, no fogginess or confusion or anything like that. I like to make sure I stay sharp!
Have you or your wife noticed that these little slip-ups, like forgetting appointments or bills, are happening more frequently now than they were, say, a year or two ago?

Well, um... I suppose if you really look at it, maybe they have picked up just a tiny bit lately. But I wouldn't say it's anything drastic! It's just... well, I retired from my handyman work about a year and two months ago, and I think that's when it started to become more noticeable. 

When I was working, I had such a set routine, you know? But since I retired, I've just been trying so hard to fill my days and be helpful around the house and in the community. I think I just took on a little too much all at once without having that strict schedule to keep me in line. It's perfectly natural to have an adjustment period after a big life change like retirement, don't you think? I'm sure once I get a better handle on my new routine, these little slip-ups will smooth right out. I really am trying my best to stay on top of things!
Have you noticed any times, even briefly, where your thoughts feel jumbled or you feel like you are not quite yourself, even if it is just for a few minutes at a time?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've never had anything like that happen, thank goodness. I always feel like myself, a hundred percent of the time. My thoughts don't really get... jumbled up in that way. 

I mean, sure, I might get a little sidetracked if I'm trying to juggle too many chores at once, but I always know exactly what I'm doing and who I am. I like to think I've still got a pretty good head on my shoulders! That's a good sign, isn't it? I'd be awfully worried if I started feeling like I wasn't quite myself, but no, I'm just regular old me, all day long. I promise you that.

Looking back over the last two years, would you say that your ability to manage your daily tasks, such as paying bills or keeping track of appointments, has noticeably declined, or does it feel about the same as it was before you retired?

Well, um... I wouldn't really use the word 'declined,' exactly. That makes it sound so... so serious, doesn't it? I'd say it's more just a few little oversights. 

Lately, I guess I have been forgetting a couple of things here and there. Like, um, returning calls from the community center, or... oh, sometimes I'll show up and realize I forgot to bring the supplies I promised for the garden group. And, well, I suppose I might miss paying a bill every now and then until my wife reminds me. She's an absolute angel about catching those little things, really. 

But it's nothing I can't handle! I just get so wrapped up in trying to help out everywhere that things slip my mind for a moment. That's pretty common when you're trying to stay active and helpful, right? I really am still doing my best to keep everything running smoothly.
Are there specific times of day, such as late in the afternoon or evening, when you find it harder to manage these tasks or feel more easily distracted than you do in the morning?

Well, um... I can't say I've really noticed a specific time of day being any worse than another. I try to keep a pretty steady pace from morning till night, just doing what I can to be useful. 

I suppose... maybe by the evening, after I've been running around helping out all day, I might be a tiny bit more tired? But that's just normal fatigue, isn't it? Anyone would be a little less sharp after a busy day of volunteering and doing chores. I wouldn't say I get more distracted, just... well, ready to relax a bit. I always try to tackle the important things early on when I'm fresh, anyway. That's the responsible way to handle it, don't you think? I really do try to manage my time well.

Have you ever had any blood work or medical tests, such as an MRI or CT scan of your brain, that your doctor ordered to specifically look into these changes in your memory or ability to stay on track?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. My regular doctor hasn't ordered any big tests like an MRI or a CT scan or anything. I think... well, I think they know I'm generally in pretty good shape for my age! 

I haven't really brought up these little slip-ups to them, to be honest. It didn't seem worth making a fuss over, you know? Just standard getting older and being busy. I'm sure if there was something really wrong, they would have noticed during my regular check-ups and ordered some blood work then. But they haven't felt the need to. That means I'm doing okay, doesn't it? I always try to take good care of my health, so I'd hate to think I missed something important.

So I'll just wander off to take care of those right quick, you know, to be extra helpful. And then, well... I suppose I do end up leaving the rest of the chores sitting there unfinished. 

It’s a little embarrassing to admit, if I'm being honest. My wife does have to remind me about the tools and the sweeping. I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or careless! I really do mean well, I just try to do too many good deeds at once and get a little sidetracked. That’s fairly normal for a fellow my age with a lot on his plate, wouldn't you say?
